subject: chemistry
question_text: Calculate the mass of Na₂CO₃ required to prepare 250 mL of 0.5 N solution.

verification.note: Chapter 5 (Stoichiometry) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.66-72), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. This chapter has NO Long Answer section in the book, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Equivalent weight and formula
steps.why: This is the normality formula rearranged for weight. Na₂CO₃ reacts with two H⁺ (its acidity is 2), so its equivalent weight is 106/2 = 53.
common_mistakes: Using GMW 106 in place of GEW 53. The question says 0.5 N, not 0.5 M.
Using 250 instead of 250/1000. The volume must be in litres inside this form.
steps.memory_tip: N for normality pairs with equivalent weight; M for molarity pairs with molar mass. Match the letter to the weight.
steps.margin_note: GEW = 53 with the division by 2 shown earns this mark.

steps.label: The answer with its unit
steps.why: 0.5 equivalents per litre in a quarter litre means 0.125 equivalents, and 0.125 × 53 = 6.625 g.
common_mistakes: Answering 13.25 g by using the molar mass route for an N question.
Dropping the unit g from the final line.
steps.memory_tip: Half strength, quarter volume: one eighth of 53 is 6.625.

insider_note: The N in 0.5 N is the whole question — it forces the equivalent weight 53. The doubled answer 13.25 g from using 106 is the standard lost mark.
